name: Pinnacle Security Stab-Resistant Undershirt
description:
A tight-fitting undershirt woven with para-aramid fibers that provide certified stab and slash resistance. The fabric is layered in a crosshatch pattern that catches and distributes the force of edged weapons across a wider area. The shirt covers torso and upper arms.

Standard issue for patrol officers and private security working in the Gray Zone districts where bladed weapons are more common than firearms. The Stab-Resistant Undershirt doesn't stop bullets and doesn't pretend to — it stops the knife you didn't see coming.
functionality: Stab and slash resistance, torso and upper arm coverage
what_it_says: You work where people carry blades and you've accepted that one of those blades is eventually aimed at you.
story_hooks: A stab-resistant undershirt shows a cut pattern that partially penetrated the para-aramid — whatever blade was used is sharper than anything the fabric was rated to stop.

physical_description.visual_profile: A form-fitting tactical base layer that hugs the torso and upper arms, presenting a sleek, utilitarian silhouette. The crosshatch weave creates subtle geometric texture across the chest and shoulders, catching light in a distinctive diamond pattern. Reads as professional security wear—understated but unmistakably protective.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit, conforming closely to the body without restricting movement. Sleeves extend to mid-bicep. The tightness is functional rather than fashionable, designed to keep the para-aramid layers flush against the skin for maximum force distribution.
physical_description.primary_material: Para-aramid synthetic blend (likely Kevlar or equivalent), woven in reinforced crosshatch lattice. The fibers have a subtle sheen, pale gray to off-white with darker thread accents showing the weave pattern.
physical_description.texture: Smooth at first touch but with pronounced crosshatch embossing visible on close inspection. The weave creates a subtle raised diamond grid across the fabric surface. Fabric is dense and slightly stiff compared to standard cotton or synthetic blends, with minimal stretch.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale gray or cream base with darker charcoal or matte-black thread highlights defining the crosshatch pattern. No graphics or branding—utilitarian anonymity. Some units feature subtle reflective safety striping on shoulders.
physical_description.closures: None; fitted pullover design. Crew neck or mock-neck collar, seamless construction to avoid pressure points.
distinctive_features: Visible crosshatch weave pattern creating force-distribution geometry
Reinforced stitching at seams and stress points
Subtle sizing labels only—no corporate branding
Optional shoulder tabs for integrated gear attachment
Seamless torso panel to prevent blade catch points
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3: Corporately subsidized security personnel. Expensive enough to indicate formal employment, not black-market or improvised.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by licensed patrol officers, private security contractors, and corpo bodyguards in mid-tier districts. Signals institutional affiliation and acceptable violence (sanctioned protective equipment). Common in the Gray Zone districts where street-level blade combat is a recognized hazard.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new and regularly maintained. With use, subtle wear on collar and cuffs, possible light staining (blood washes out easily). Never visibly damaged—replacement is standard when integrity is compromised.
